text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You presented with weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; to begin my evaluation, have you noticed if these symptoms started suddenly or developed gradually over time?

text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. Given your history of anabolic steroid use, chronic alcohol consumption, and recent significant weight loss, have you noticed any muscle atrophy (shrinking) in your right arm compared to the left?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Brachial Plexopathy due to Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma.

The combination of progressive right arm weakness, sensory loss, significant unexplained weight loss, and your history of alcohol use and anabolic steroid use is highly suspicious for a malignancy causing a Pancoast tumor or metastatic involvement of the brachial plexus. I need to visualize your chest and abdomen immediately. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray, Abdominal_CTA. REQUEST TEST: CA 19-9.
